children: Australia's central bank may have to raise interest rates for a fourth time this year if inflation proves stronger than expected, a top official said on Tuesday.

Speaking at a property conference, Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter also said the policy board was aiming to cool the economy down through higher rates, but played down the risk of a possible recession.
"I think the board has been pretty clear...that inflation is a top priority right now," said Hunter, who heads the RBA's economics unit.
"We are concerned about inflation and if there is a sense that inflation is going to be stronger...the board may well have to raise interest rates for that."

A stubbornly high inflation reading for July has led markets to wager a 70% probability the RBA will hike by 25 basis points to 4.60% at its policy meeting on September 29, up from less than 10% a month ago. Markets even see a 60% chance rates will reach 4.85% next year. (0#AUDIRPR)
Surveys on Tuesday underlined the damage rate concerns and rising fuel bills caused by the conflict in the Gulf were doing to confidence in the economy.
A NAB measure of business conditions sank to six-year lows in August amid a broad squeeze on profit margins, while a Westpac-MI index of consumer sentiment reversed sharply in September.
Hunter said the RBA wanted to see a softening in consumer demand in order to bring demand in the economy better into line with constrained supply.
She noted past rate rises had slowed the housing market and sent prices lower in most major cities, but she did not expect to see a "recession or anything like that".
